hook: Greenland looks as big as Africa. It's fourteen times smaller.

beats.narration: Greenland looks as big as Africa. It's fourteen times smaller.
beats.claim: Africa is about 14 times the size of Greenland.

beats.narration: Greenland is about 2.17 million square kilometres. Africa is 30.37 million.
beats.claim: Greenland is 2.166 million km²; Africa is 30.37 million km².

beats.narration: Africa could hold the USA, China and India, with room to spare.
beats.claim: US 9.867M + China 9.597M + India 3.287M = 22.75M km², less than Africa's 30.37M km².

beats.narration: The culprit is the Mercator map, made in 1569 for sailors.
beats.claim: The Mercator projection was introduced by Gerardus Mercator in 1569.

beats.narration: It keeps compass directions as straight lines. The price: everything near the poles gets stretched.
beats.claim: On the Mercator projection, lines of constant bearing are straight lines, but area is distorted.

beats.narration: Africa sits on the equator, so it barely stretches. Greenland sits near the pole, so it balloons.
beats.claim: Because Africa straddles the equator its Mercator size stays nearly true, while areas far from the equator are enlarged.

beats.narration: Slide Greenland down to the equator, and watch it shrink.

title: Greenland looks as big as Africa. It's 14 times smaller.
description: Why the map on your classroom wall makes Greenland look huge.
